Product Data Analyst

What would you be doing here?

As a Product Data Analyst, you'll be the go-to data partner for our Product organization. You'll collaborate closely with Product Managers, Engineers, Marketing, and Business teams to build trusted metrics, enable self-serve analytics, and uncover insights that drive product decisions.

Drive data across the organization:

40767085b6cd031e.description: Own a feature from the database to the browser, and prove it works. We hire for ability, not years. Read the whole description before you apply. Before you apply Were direct about how we work. Read this section first. We value engineers who know what they dont know, and say so. If youre honest about your gaps, well invest in closing them. If you hide weaknesses or oversell your experience, you wont last here. We expect you to use AI coding tools. Everyone here does, and pretending otherwise in 2026 would be theatre. What we care about is what happens next. Roughly two in five lines of committed code across the industry are now AI-written, while fewer than half of developers say they always verify that code before committing it, and in a controlled security study 45 percent of AI-generated samples introduced a vulnerability from the OWASP top ten. The failure mode is specific, and it is not sloppiness. AI code arrives with clean syntax and consistent naming, so the signals that used to make bad code obvious are gone. What hides underneath is a misunderstood requirement or an edge case nobody considered. Reading it for style tells you nothing. You have to work out what the change was supposed to do and then check whether it does that. So the skill we hire for is not typing and it is not prompting. It is knowing when you are done. You can delegate the work. You cannot delegate the accountability. We are also not going to tell you that AI makes everyone ten times faster. The one properly controlled study on this found experienced developers were 19 percent slower with AI while believing they had been faster, and the follow-up could not be completed because developers refused to work without the tools. The productivity question is genuinely open. The verification cost is the part that has actually been measured. We move fast. Growth happens outside comfort zones. If this sounds harsh, were probably not a fit. If it sounds like the environment youve been looking for, keep reading. The role Allerin builds AI and IoT products: edge to cloud video intelligence, computer vision systems, and data platforms. We also partner with select clients to solve their hardest technical problems. Youll do both. Youll work across a Rails API backend and a React admin frontend, on a production system with roughly 160 models, 231 controllers, and five separate API surfaces covering dashboard, mobile, valet, kiosk, and AI/ML integrations. This is not greenfield. You are joining a system that already has users, and the work is to extend it without breaking what runs. Location: Navi Mumbai Team: Engineering Works alongside: the Backend Team Lead, who owns architecture, and the test automation engineer, who owns the automated suites What youll own Features, end to end Take a feature from schema and migration through the API to the React screen a person actually uses, and stay with it after it ships. Design endpoints with clean contracts, sensible pagination, consistent errors, and no surprises for the clients that consume them. Write the tests that would catch your own mistake, not the tests that pass. The surfaces where AI meets a person Build the screens where a models output reaches a human: review and override queues, confidence shown honestly, audit trails of who decided what. Treat a prediction as a probability rather than a fact. A vision model at 97 percent confidence is still wrong often enough that the interface has to say so. Make the numbers visible. If a client is told false positives fell 85 percent, something you built is where that number comes from. Verification Know what you ran, what it proved, and what it did not. "The tests pass" is the beginning of that sentence, not the end of it. Review AI-written changes, including your own, for intent rather than style. Break your own work before someone else does, and say plainly when it is not ready. A codebase you did not write Read code, git history, and other peoples decisions before changing them. Ask why something is the way it is before deciding it is wrong. Occasionally it is wrong, and then you fix it properly. What we expect you can do We dont count years.
